landing.ctaBody: Start with one laptop. The branches follow.
landing.ctaTitle: Plant your first tree in ten minutes
landing.featureAssistantBody: Ask in plain words, or tell it where you just signed in. Every change waits for your approval.
landing.featureCheckBody: Sign-ins not confirmed for 30 days, or marked by you, wait in one list.
landing.featureMapBody: Each account as a tree, from the device it started on to every CLI, app and browser profile it reached. Nothing overlaps.
landing.featurePaletteBody: Jump to any device, profile or account from the keyboard.
landing.featureTeamBody: Keep a personal map, or share one with your team as admin, editor or viewer.
landing.featureThemes: Light and dark themes, in Indonesian and English.
landing.featureWhereBody: Open any account to see every place it is signed in, and where it was signed out.
landing.featuresTitle: Built for people with too many accounts
landing.footer: © {year} AkunMu. The trees of where you're signed in.
landing.heroAnnotLeaf: Leaf · a CLI on the server
landing.heroBody: Many Google accounts, a few laptops, a CLI that signed in with a code from another browser. AkunMu draws the tree: where each account first signed in, where it grew to, and which leaves need a look. So you always know where to sign out.
landing.heroNote: No passwords, no browser extension, no tracking.
landing.heroTitle: See every account, from its roots to its leaves.
landing.howTitle: From the roots to the leaves
landing.metaDescription: AkunMu draws a tree for every account: the device it started on, the devices it reached with a code, link or QR code, and the browser profiles, apps and CLIs it is signed in to. No passwords stored.
landing.metaTitle: The trees of where your accounts are signed in
landing.privacyBody: AkunMu is a map, not a vault. It records places (devices, browser profiles, apps) and the names accounts sign in with. That is all it needs to tell you where to sign out.
landing.privacyPoint1: No passwords, recovery codes, one-time codes or cookies are ever stored.
landing.privacyPoint2: Notes that look like a secret are refused before they are saved.
landing.privacyPoint3: Each workspace is isolated by row-level security in the database.
landing.privacyPoint4: The assistant only proposes changes; nothing happens until you approve.
landing.privacyTitle: Built to never hold your passwords
landing.shotAssistantAlt: AkunMu's assistant answering where a Claude account is signed in
landing.shotCheckAlt: AkunMu's list of sign-ins to check, grouped by device
landing.shotColumnsAlt: AkunMu's columns: a server, its places, and the account signed in there
landing.shotTreeAlt: AkunMu's account trees: a Claude account rooted on a home PC, with a CLI on a server let in with a code
landing.showAssistantBody: “Where is my Claude account signed in?” It answers from your trees, and every change waits for your yes.
landing.showCheckBody: Everything not confirmed for 30 days, grouped by device. Confirm a whole laptop at once.
landing.showColumnsBody: Device, then place, then the accounts signed in there, each with how it got in.
landing.showColumnsTitle: Columns: what is on this laptop
landing.showTreeBody: Point at a leaf to light up where it came from and what grew from it. A CLI let in with a code hangs on the browser that approved it.
landing.showcaseTitle: One workspace, four ways to look
landing.step1Body: Record where an account was signed in first: the laptop and the browser profile.
landing.step2Body: Signed in on another device with a code, a magic link or a QR code? Note where it came from.
landing.step3Body: Leaves wilt after 30 days without a look. Confirm what is still signed in and sign out the rest.
